title: Service Steward Sprint Map and Risk Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This working doc consolidates a 90-day sprint map for Service Stewards (owners of service dependability), plus a lightweight risk playbook to guide cross-functional decisions when service-level objectives (SLOs) drift or incidents threaten customer impact. Treat as an operational canvas: living notes, runbook inputs, and a checklist for rollouts and rollbacks.

Context and scope:
- Audience: service stewards, product owners, platform/infra, runtime engineers, SRE on-call, solutions engineering
- Scope: primary focus on inference-serving pipelines (API surface, model routing, KV cache, batching), downstream observability, and cross-region routing policies; includes both feature launches and slow degradations that accumulate into customer-visible impact.
- Non-goal: detailed per-service code changes. This is about orchestration, measurement, and decision gates.

How to use this doc (quick):
1) Read the 90-day map and align owners for each milestone.
2) Add service-specific metrics into the dashboard list and tag jira backlog items with SRE- tagging.
3) If SLO signal crosses warning threshold, run the Incident Triage checklist below and escalate per the playbook.

90-day sprint map (high level):
- Week 0 (alignment): identify 6 priority services, confirm service steward (owner) for each, baseline SLI definitions, and wire metrics to the central SRE dashboard. Deliverable: "service-steward-register" (spreadsheet). Owner: Aisha K.
- Weeks 1–3 (baseline & quick wins): capture current p99/p95 latency distributions, 5xx rates, and cache hit ratios; enable prefix caching for top-3 hot endpoints as experiment. Deliverable: quick-win runbooks + dashboard tiles. Owners: Miguel (runtime), Riley (observability).
- Weeks 4–7 (policy & playbook): define throttling/fallback policies per service, test automated fallback to smaller model variant in staging, and create canary rollout criteria. Deliverable: policy config templates + canary checklist. Owner: Dana (platform).
- Weeks 8–11 (capacity & chaos): run capacity tabletop & controlled chaos (simulated cold-starts and KV eviction scenarios), measure SLO error budget consumption. Deliverable: chaos experiment report + remediation backlog. Owner: Evan (SRE).
- Weeks 12–13 (cutover & handoff): finalize runbooks, conduct cross-team dry-run, and hand off to steady-state stewards with weekly pulse checks for 30 days. Deliverable: handoff notes + 30d pulse calendar. Owner: Aisha.

Operational acceptance criteria (for each service):
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail latency for streaming, 5xx rate, error budget burn rate over last 30d, cache hit ratio, and median token cost.
- Thresholds to define per service: green (<10% monthly error budget used), amber (10–40%), red (>40% or >1% increase in 5xx vs baseline).
- Canary: <5% traffic during canary, <1% additional error-budget burn, and no regressions in user-facing quality checks.

Incident & triage checklist (quick):
1) Observe: Service steward or on-call sees amber/red signal on dashboard. Post to #sre-service-stewards with short summary.
2) Confirm: Check instrumented traces (sampled), compare baseline histograms, verify if it's a regression or expected drift.
3) Contain: If customer-facing, apply policy: route to fallback model variant OR temporarily increase dedicated pool capacity (if reserved capacity available).
4) Investigate: Capture KV cache eviction events, batching latency spikes, kernel GPU saturation, or slow external dependency.
5) Communicate: Standup sync within 30 minutes if red, update status page if customer impact.
6) Remediate & rewind: If mitigations applied, monitor 30m window before scaling down mitigations.
7) Postmortem & action items: capture RCA and assign remediation tickets within 5 working days.

Risk playbook (short):
- Risk categories: infrastructure saturation, model regression, telemetry blindspots, config rollback risk, cross-region replication lag.
- Fast mitigations (seconds–minutes): traffic reroute, circuit break on heavy endpoints, fallback to CPU-quantized model variant, increase ephemeral burst capacity.
- Medium mitigations (minutes–hours): scale dedicated pool, restart model worker set with newer kernel flags reversed, or toggle KV cache TTLs to reduce thrash.
- Slow mitigations (days–weeks): re-training/re-onboarding of model, code patch for memory leak, or changes to kernel selection algorithms.

Decision matrix for rollback vs mitigation:
- If customer-facing latency >2x p95 or error rate >2x baseline AND mitigation doesn't reduce within 20 minutes -> rollback to earlier stable model/config.
- If only internal degradations (e.g., CPU >80% but no user errors), trigger medium mitigation path and monitor.
- If uncertain: prefer short-term mitigation and schedule a rapid review within 2 hours with product and SRE.

Telemetry & dashboards (minimal required tiles):
- SLI panel: p50/p95/p99 per route, token time per token, streaming tail duration.
- Error panel: 5xx by code, client errors, backend errors, and error budget burn chart (30d).
- Resource panel: GPU utilization, batch size distribution, KV cache hit/miss rates, memory GC events.
- Quality panel: hallucination/regression alerts tied to prompt test-suite (monthly sample).

Runbook excerpts (copy-paste friendly):
- Quick reroute: set routing weight to fallback cluster = 100% for route X. Monitor 5m.
- Clear KV cache safely: run phased eviction on non-primary shard then verify hit ratio recovery.
- Canary rollback: abort canary, scale down canary workers, and restore previous routing weights.

Cross-functional dependencies and contacts:
- Runtime (kernel/ops): Miguel Santos — primary for experiment changes.
- Observability: Riley Chen — dashboards, alert tuning.
- Platform & Autoscale: Dana Ortiz — policies and capacity changes.
- SRE & Incident Lead: Evan Brooks — triage and postmortems.
- Product Liaison (per service): listed on service-steward register.
- Communication channels: #sre-service-stewards (Slack), oncall@sre (email).

Open questions / notes to self:
- How to standardize token-cost SLO across services that use different model families? (Action: proposal due Week 3.)
- Do we need a separate canary lane for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints? (Experiment request)
- Confirm budget for short-term burst capacity in Dedicated — finance sign-off pending.

Next steps (this week):
- Create service-steward-register and invite POs + stewards (owner: Aisha).
- Instrument missing p99 tiles for top 6 services (owner: Riley).
- Draft token-cost normalization proposal (owner: Miguel).

Appendix: quick links and templates
- Service steward register template: /spreadsheets/service-steward-register (create in Drive)
- Canary checklist (template): add to linked artifacts and tag in PRs
- Postmortem template: /confluence/SRE/postmortem-template

Draft status: rough operational plan with experiments scheduled. Expect edits as services report baseline numbers.
